in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have a child (or children) that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do! I have one child, Alex, who's 8 years old and lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know you have Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with you in the UK.

To continue assessing your eligibility, can you tell me: Are you the person responsible for Alex? By this I mean, are you the one who is mainly responsible for looking after Alex on a day-to-day basis (such as providing their care, making sure they have food, clothing, and shelter)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I'm Alex's parent and I'm responsible for looking after them day-to-day - making sure they have everything they need, food, clothes, all of that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful information.

Now, could you tell me: Are you or Alex currently living in the UK? And do you (or your partner, if you have one) have the right to claim Child Benefit - meaning, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, indefinite leave to remain, or another immigration status that would allow you to claim benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we're both living in the UK. I'm a UK citizen, so I have the right to claim benefits.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment.

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex? For example, Alex's other parent or another person?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One more important question: Do you or your partner (if you have one) have individual income over £50,000 per year? This is relevant because there's a High Income Child Benefit Charge that may apply if either of you earns above this threshold.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of us earns over £50,000 a year, so that shouldn't be an issue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- You are responsible for Alex's day-to-day care
- Both you and Alex live in the UK
- You are a UK citizen with the right to claim benefits
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Neither you nor your partner earns over £50,000 per year

You meet all the requirements for Child Benefit. You can proceed with making a claim if you haven't already done so. If you need help with the application process, you can apply online through the government's official channels or by post.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
